title: Allowed Rate by Pricing Structure — Residential Natural Gas Supply Energy Lines
content:
**Rule.** For the energy line of the most recent bill on a Residential Natural Gas Supply agreement, the rate the plan allows for the line's cycle depends on the plan's pricing structure: on a capped variable plan it is the lower of the variable rate in force for the cycle and the contract rate, which is the plan's ceiling; on a month-to-month variable plan it is the variable rate in force for the cycle; on a fixed plan it is the contract rate. The correct amount of the line is its billed therms multiplied by that allowed rate, rounded half up to the cent.

**Variable rate in force.** The variable rate in force for the cycle is the new rate of the most recent variable rate change notice on the agreement — the one with the latest effective date — which within this rule's scope took effect on or before the cycle's billing period start after timely notice.

### Decision table

| Plan's pricing structure | Allowed rate for the cycle |
|---|---|
| capped variable | the lower of the variable rate in force and the contract rate |
| variable (month-to-month) | the variable rate in force |
| fixed | the contract rate |

### Worked figures (hypothetical line of 112 therms; contract rate 0.7950)

| Pricing structure | Variable rate in force | Allowed rate | Correct amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| capped variable | 0.8400 | 0.7950 | 89.04 |
| capped variable | 0.7600 | 0.7600 | 85.12 |
| variable (month-to-month) | 0.8400 | 0.8400 | 94.08 |
| fixed | 0.8400 | 0.7950 | 89.04 |

The records read are the plan's pricing structure, the agreement's contract rate, the variable rate change notices on the agreement, and the therms of the line.
